article.title: Why LA Progressive Is Changing Its Voter Guide Recommendation to Colin Hernandez
article.author: Sharon Kyle
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. LA Progressive has updated its Progressive Voter Guide for California’s 51st Assembly District, replacing Rick Chavez Zbur with Colin Hernandez. A reader recently asked us to revisit this race, pointing to a contradiction between our publication’s defense of free expression and Zbur’s role as a lead author of Assembly Bill 715. That request deserved a serious response. Our voter guide is intended to help readers make informed choices. When readers raise substantive concerns about its contents, we have a responsibility to examine them—and to make changes when the evidence warrants it. Readers ultimately decide which candidates best represent their values and priorities. AB 715, signed into law in October 2025, was presented as a measure to combat antisemitism and discrimination in California schools. Protecting Jewish students from harassment and discrimination is essential. The question is whether the law’s approach adequately protects freedom of expression alongside that obligation. ACLU California Action opposed AB 715, warning that it could chill constitutionally protected classroom discussion and undermine academic freedom. These concerns deserve particular attention when teachers discuss Israel, Palestine, and human rights—subjects on which political criticism must not automatically be treated as discrimination. The law permits members of the public, including anonymous complainants, to file complaints alleging that instructional materials violate its antidiscrimination requirements, provided they supply evidence or information leading to evidence. That does not mean mentioning Gaza is itself prohibited. Our concern is that a broad complaint process can encourage educators to avoid difficult subjects rather than risk an investigation. In an article published by LA Progressive, civil liberties attorney Stephen Rohde examined the First Amendment concerns surrounding AB 715 and the danger of conflating criticism of Israel with antisemitism. His analysis underscores a principle central to our coverage: protecting students from discrimination and protecting political expression are obligations that must be upheld together. Hernandez’s published platform explicitly opposes AB 715 and calls for protecting teachers’ academic freedom. He also supports universal healthcare through CalCare, expanded social housing, stronger tenant protections, universal childcare, and greater contributions from billionaires and large corporations. His immigration platform calls for abolishing ICE and expanding access to legal representation for people facing deportation. These positions explain his inclusion in the updated guide. They reflect an approach that treats housing, healthcare, education, and human dignity as public responsibilities and provide readers with substantive differences to consider in this race. Our voter guide should reflect careful examination of the candidates and the issues. That requires a willingness to listen, revisit earlier judgments, and explain changes openly. We thank the reader who brought these concerns to our attention. The updated entry for California’s 51st Assembly District now lists Colin Hernandez.
